record.title_md: [Open problem: true ordered Ramsey number of matchings](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.5292)

dossier_meta.catalog_title: Open problem: true ordered Ramsey number of matchings
dossier_meta.statement_text: What is the true ordered Ramsey number of an ordered matching $M$ on $n$ vertices? Theorem 1.1 gives the lower bound $r_<(M) \geq n^{c\log n/\log\log n}$ for some labeling, while Theorem 1.2 gives $r_<(M) \leq n^{\lceil \log n \rceil}$; the authors describe the upper bound as 'almost matching' but the gap remains open.
dossier_meta.context_text: For ordinary matchings the Ramsey number is clearly linear, but for ordered matchings the paper shows the ordered Ramsey number can be superpolynomial. The precise exponent (between $c\log n/\log\log n$ and $\log n$) is not determined.
